# XTRM UI

## Overview

`xtrm-ui` owns XTRM's Pi header, editor density, themes, and tool presentation.
It decorates Pi's native execution rather than replacing tool execution or rewriting
model-facing results.

`custom-footer` is the sole footer owner. `xtrm-ui` never calls `setFooter()`.

## Credits

The original theme palette and header layout were derived from
[pi-dex](https://github.com/mariozechner/lemmy/tree/main/packages/pi-dex) by
[@mariozechner](https://github.com/mariozechner). Write/edit previews are inspired
by **@heyhuynhgiabuu/pi-diff**. The current implementation and theme identifiers
are XTRM-owned; neither project is loaded as UI execution plumbing.

## Themes

The extension discovers four themes:

- `xtrm-dark`
- `xtrm-light`
- `xtrm-dark-flattools`
- `xtrm-light-flattools`

`toolRowBg: false` selects the matching `-flattools` theme. Legacy `pidex-*` values
in Pi settings or persisted session preferences are migrated to the equivalent
`xtrm-*` value.

## Tool Rendering

Native tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `find`, and `ls`) retain
Pi's execute functions and use `ToolRenderContext` for arguments, state, errors,
and timing. Their rows use one tree shape:

```text
• grep renderResult
  └ first matching line
    next matching line
    showing 6/94 matchs (ctrl+o expand) · 1.6s · 247B
```

Collapsed native rows show up to six output lines. Bash keeps the latest six;
read, new-file write, grep, find, and ls keep the first six. Edit and updated-file
write retain their 18-line diff preview. Small results render in full without an
expansion hint.

External tools use one background-row renderer with provider badges for Serena,
GitNexus, structured-return, process, and generic tools. Their collapsed output is
bounded and retains the `└─` metadata footer. Ctrl+O reveals hidden content.
Rendering does not mutate tool-result payloads.

Code-carrying tools (`codemode`, `python`) keep the `● used <tool>` header
unchanged but render the body like native bash rows: bold execution lines with
their own hidden-count, output hung off a muted `└` tree, and a plain dim meta
footer. Execution and result cap independently (`commandPreviewLines` and
`extPreviewLines`), so a long program never starves its output.

Pending tools have no metadata footer. Expansion hints appear only when content is hidden.

## Preferences

Only active, user-controlled behavior is persisted:

| Preference | Default | Command |
|---|---|---|
| `themeName` | `xtrm-dark` | `/xtrm-ui-theme dark\|light` |
| `density` | `compact` | `/xtrm-ui-density compact\|comfortable` |
| `showHeader` | `true` | `/xtrm-ui-header on\|off` |
| `forceTheme` | `true` | `/xtrm-ui-forcetheme on\|off` |
| `toolRowBg` | `false` | `/xtrm-ui-rowbg on\|off` |

Tools start collapsed. Hidden thinking blocks use an empty placeholder. These are
fixed presentation choices rather than persisted preferences.

## Commands

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `/xtrm-ui` | Show active preferences, model, and context usage |
| `/xtrm-ui-theme dark\|light` | Switch the XTRM theme family |
| `/xtrm-ui-density compact\|comfortable` | Change editor horizontal padding |
| `/xtrm-ui-header on\|off` | Toggle the XTRM header |
| `/xtrm-ui-forcetheme on\|off` | Enable or disable XTRM theme ownership |
| `/xtrm-ui-rowbg on\|off` | Toggle native tool-row backgrounds |
| `/xtrm-ui-reset` | Restore the five defaults above |

Obsolete result-compaction and external-chrome commands are intentionally not
registered. External tools always use the unified background renderer.

## Install and Migration

Canonical source lives under `packages/pi-extensions/` and is exposed by the
managed `@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions` package. Before Pi reads its configured theme,
launch preflight symlinks the four XTRM-owned theme files into `~/.pi/agent/themes`.
The extension still discovers its package-local theme directory after startup.

Runtime sync removes the obsolete UI package entry. It migrates legacy theme names
and removes the retired `xtrmExternalCompact` setting in project settings; user-global
preferences are migrated only during global runtime sync. Unrelated Pi settings remain
unchanged.
